concepts.label: OnUpdate handler
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the mutation-triggered JavaScript entry point (`function OnUpdate(doc, meta) {...}`) that fires on document creation/mutation in the Listen to Location keyspace; the core worked-example primitive this whole batch is built on

concepts.label: Bucket binding (with Read Only / Read and Write permission)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a specific sub-type of the sibling batch's eventing:binding concept; a Function-scoped alias bound to a bucket/scope/collection, gated to Read Only or Read and Write, which is what makes cross-collection writes from a handler possible

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a handler's binding to a source keyspace's mutation stream; distinct from dependsOnService (service-level) and requiresSetting (config field)
relations.evidence: The `OnUpdate` JavaScript handler listens to mutations or data changes within a specified source collection.

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a handler mutating a keyspace through a bound alias rather than its own listened-to collection; captures the cross-collection fan-out pattern this page demonstrates

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a hard constraint on the metadata keyspace during the Function's deployed lifecycle state; distinct from behavesDifferentlyUnder because this is a prohibition, not a change in behavior
relations.evidence: Do not add, modify, or delete documents in the Eventing storage keyspace `rr100.eventing.metadata` while your Eventing Functions are in a deployed state.

notable_absence.finding: This worked example walks through creating, deploying, and testing an Eventing Function end to end (buckets, bindings, JavaScript, deploy, test) and names no privilege, capella-role, or credential type gate anywhere - consistent with the three core lifecycle pages in the sibling batch (add/deploy/manage), which found the same absence.

cross_component_finding: The two examples on this page (create-in-target vs update-in-source) are distinguished purely by which bucket binding permission is Read Only vs Read and Write and which alias the handler writes back into (`tgt[meta.id]=doc` vs `src[meta.id]=doc`) - no separate concept or setting exists for 'enrich-in-place' vs 'enrich-into-new-collection'; it's the same eventing:on-update-handler primitive composed differently with the eventing:bucket-binding permission model already established in add-eventing-functions.json.
